title: Math: The Place Value 🔟
summary:
1. Tens and Ones
We can group numbers into Tens (groups of 10) and Ones (singles).
• Example: 34 is 3 Tens (30) and 4 Ones (4).

2. Compose and Decompose
We can break numbers apart or put them together.
• 50 + 2 = 52
• 87 = 80 + 7

3. Comparing Numbers
To find which number is greater (bigger), always look at the Tens place first!
• 72 is greater than 59 because 7 tens is more than 5 tens.

4. Rounding to the Nearest 10
Look at the Ones digit to round a number:
• If it ends in 1, 2, 3, 4 ➔ Round DOWN (Stay in the same ten. 32 ➔ 30).
• If it ends in 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 ➔ Round UP (Go to the next ten. 38 ➔ 40).
